summary: Jest suite runs cleanly (62 files, 633 tests) with high overall coverage (96.51% statements/lines, 98.42% functions, 86.37% branches); unit/integration/e2e scripts are segregated, and traceability annotations are common with one missing-supports gap.
reasoning: Test execution is stable: `npm test` and `npm test -- --coverage` both pass with 62 suites and 633 tests, showing the suite is runnable and consistent.
Coverage is strong overall (96.51% statements/lines, 98.42% functions, 86.37% branches) and meets configured global thresholds, reducing broad untested-surface risk.

Branch coverage is notably weaker in key orchestration and helper paths (e.g., `src/index.ts` at 36.66% branches and `src/rules/require-traceability.ts` at 44.44%), indicating conditional logic is less exercised than line/function coverage suggests.

Tests are largely behavioral: RuleTester cases validate lint outputs and autofixes, CLI integration uses real ESLint invocation via `spawnSync`, and E2E exercises full workflows with temp workspaces, improving real-world confidence.

Testing debt: one suite lacks any @supports annotation (`tests/maintenance/storyParser.test.ts`), and there is only a single E2E test file, leaving broader end-to-end coverage thinner than unit/integration breadth.

Given high coverage, reliable execution, and strong behavioral testing with localized branch gaps and a minor traceability annotation omission, a mid‑80s score reflects a healthy suite with moderate residual risk in conditional paths and end-to-end breadth.

rationale: `package.json` defines `main`/`types` under `lib`, indicating a distributable module.
Peer dependency on `eslint` and rule-centric tests indicate an ESLint plugin library.
A CLI binary exists (`traceability-maint`), but the primary deliverable is the plugin library.

findings.message: Test file lacks any @supports annotation, reducing traceability mapping coverage for this suite.
